title: Orthogonal subspaces and restriction through a cartesian field extension
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. A norm on a $K$-vector space $V$ means a definite function $N:V\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ with $N(x+y)\le\max(N(x),N(y))$ and $N(ax)=|a|N(x)$. A finite family $v_i$ is orthogonal if $N(\sum_i a_iv_i)=\max_i|a_i|N(v_i)$ for all coefficients. (1) If $V$ has a finite orthogonal basis, every $K$-linear subspace of $V$, with the restricted norm, has an orthogonal basis. (2) Let $F/K$ be an isometric extension of such valued fields such that every finite-dimensional $K$-linear subspace of $F$ has an orthogonal $K$-basis. Let $W$ be a normed $F$-vector space (so $N(aw)=|a|_F N(w)$). If every finite-dimensional $F$-linear subspace of $W$ has an orthogonal $F$-basis, then every finite-dimensional $K$-linear subspace of $W$ has an orthogonal $K$-basis. Zero spaces are allowed, with maximum of the empty family equal to $0$.

proof.text: For clause (1), the norm satisfies $N(-v)=N(v)$ since $|-1|=1$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-trf-cartesian-subspace] hold for the given finite orthogonal basis and every $K$-subspace $U$. Its conclusion is exactly the asserted finite orthogonal basis of $U$, including $U=0$.

proof.text: For clause (2), fix a finite-dimensional $K$-subspace $U\subset W$. If $U=0$, take the empty basis. Otherwise take a finite $K$-basis $u_1,\ldots,u_m$. The space $M=\sum_{j=1}^m Fu_j\subset W$ is finite-dimensional over $F$: deleting dependent vectors from this finite spanning list gives an $F$-basis. By the hypothesis on $W$, choose an orthogonal $F$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $M$, and write $u_j=\sum_i c_{ij}e_i$ with $c_{ij}\in F$.

proof.text: For each $i$, put $A_i=\operatorname{span}_K\{c_{i1},\ldots,c_{im}\}\subset F$. It is finite-dimensional, since the displayed finite list spans it. The hypothesis on $F/K$ supplies an orthogonal $K$-basis $a_{i1},\ldots,a_{is_i}$ of $A_i$, where $s_i=0$ when $A_i=0$. Let $b_{i\ell}=a_{i\ell}e_i$ and $V_0=\operatorname{span}_K\{b_{i\ell}\}\subset W$. Each coefficient $c_{ij}$ is a $K$-linear combination of the $a_{i\ell}$, so the displayed expressions for $u_j$ show $U\subseteq V_0$.

source.place: Independent finite-coefficient argument for the imported BGR 2.4.1/5 and 2.4.3/4 input; archival source unavailable, WANTED in report. Subspace theorem supplied by lem-trf-cartesian-subspace.

proof.text: For arbitrary $d_{i\ell}\in K$, put $z_i=\sum_\ell d_{i\ell}a_{i\ell}\in F$. Orthogonality of the $e_i$ and then of each coefficient basis give $$N\left(\sum_{i,\ell}d_{i\ell}b_{i\ell}\right)=N\left(\sum_i z_ie_i\right)=\max_i |z_i|_F N(e_i)=\max_{i,\ell}|d_{i\ell}|_K|a_{i\ell}|_F N(e_i)=\max_{i,\ell}|d_{i\ell}|_K N(b_{i\ell}).$$ Here the equality $|d|_F=|d|_K$ uses the isometric embedding. Empty coefficient blocks contribute zero.

source.place: Independent finite-coefficient argument for the imported BGR 2.4.1/5 and 2.4.3/4 input; archival source unavailable, WANTED in report. Subspace theorem supplied by lem-trf-cartesian-subspace.

proof.text: Every $b_{i\ell}$ has positive norm, since $a_{i\ell}\ne0$, $e_i\ne0$, and the norm is definite. If a linear combination of the $b_{i\ell}$ is zero, the equality in Step 4 makes each $|d_{i\ell}|_K N(b_{i\ell})$ zero, hence every $d_{i\ell}=0$. Thus these vectors are linearly independent, and they span $V_0$ by its definition: they form a finite orthogonal $K$-basis. If there are no such vectors, this is the empty basis of $V_0=0$.

proof.text: The restricted norm on $V_0$ is a definite ultrametric $K$-norm: scalar homogeneity follows from $F$-homogeneity and $|a|_F=|a|_K$ for $a\in K$; symmetry follows from $|-1|=1$. Apply [lem-trf-cartesian-subspace] to its finite orthogonal basis from Step 5 and the subspace $U\subseteq V_0$ from Step 3. It gives an orthogonal $K$-basis of $U$. Since $U$ was arbitrary, clause (2) follows.

lean.statement: theorem exists_orthogonal_basis_subspace {K : Type u} [Field K] (abv : AbsoluteValue K ℝ≥0) (h_nontrivial : abv.IsNontrivial) (h_nonarch : IsNonarchimedean abv) {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (N : V → ℝ≥0) (h_definite : ∀ x : V, N x = 0 ↔ x = 0) (h_ultra : IsNonarchimedean N) (h_smul : ∀ (a : K) (x : V), N (a • x) = abv a * N x) (n : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) K V) (h_orthogonal : ∀ a : Fin n → K, N (∑ i, a i • b i) = Finset.univ.sup (fun i ↦ abv (a i) * N (b i))) (U : Submodule K V) : ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Module.Basis (Fin m) K U), ∀ a : Fin m → K, N (↑(∑ i, a i • c i) : V) = Finset.univ.sup (fun i ↦ abv (a i) * N (↑(c i) : V))
lean.note: The first declaration states clause (1); exists_orthogonal_basis_restrictScalars states clause (2). Orthogonality is the explicit finite-supremum identity in NNReal, with empty supremum zero. Norms remain unbundled functions as in the node; no completeness or global finite-dimensionality of the scalar extension or W is assumed.
